news.title: Stem Sorter: your files on the right tracks of your template, in your DAW
news.body: Stem Sorter reads the names of your recorded files, works out what each one is, and puts every one on the right track of your template. It builds a session for Studio One and REAPER, an AAF for Logic, Pro Tools, Cubase and Digital Performer, and a numbered folder with a track sheet for Ableton, FL Studio, Bitwig and Reason. The few doubtful matches go to the top in amber; fix them in a click. Normalize by peak, RMS or LUFS while you sort. $35, once. One licence, two computers.

news.title: Chordlight 88 2.0: it records, and it makes the video for you
news.body: The readout you know, and two new buttons. Rec saves the take as MIDI, as 24-bit WAV, or as a .chordlight file that reopens with the lights and the audio in sync; Keep rescues the last five minutes even when you forgot to press it. Video draws a 1080p clip, not a screen capture: your lesson title, a picture or looping video behind it, a readout plate, and the last four chords climbing away from the keys. A microphone input ducks the keys under your voice. One key, two computers, moved yourself. Free for everyone who has 1.x; $24 for everyone else while the early bird lasts, $48 after.

news.title: AMB Digital: ten precision plug-ins, one key
news.body: Where AMB Analog adds character, this gives control. Ten separate plug-ins built around one idea: you should never have to guess. The equalisers draw their curves over the real spectrum, before and after. The de-esser draws the reduction it is actually applying, measured from the audio. The delay shows its echoes travelling. Every picture is also a control surface - drag a node, a crossover, a threshold or a tap, and the panel below follows. 120 presets, twelve in each. One key unlocks all ten, on two computers. $39.

news.title: Hub 1.3.0: What's new, artwork, and a switch you control
news.body: This page is the new part. Releases, new apps and notes from the studio land here, and the sidebar marks itself when one does. Every app in the library now shows its own artwork, drawn from the same place the store draws it, so the two can no longer drift. And there is a switch on the library page for usage notes: it is off until you turn it on, it records which app you open and whether this is a Windows or a Mac, and it never reads a file name, a folder, a project or anything inside an app. You can delete everything it has ever sent, from any computer, in one press.

news.title: Nebula Tide 2.1, and it runs on Android now
news.body: Version 2.1 is up for Windows and Mac, and for the first time there is an Android build on the site. It is the same app: pay what you want, no key, no account needed to run it. If you already have Nebula Tide 2 the Hub will offer the update; if you are still on version 1, this replaces it rather than sitting beside it. macOS needs Big Sur or newer - a Catalina machine cannot run this one.

news.title: PerformLive is back, on 0.4.1
news.body: The download is open again, for Windows and Mac. If you installed the last beta the Hub will offer you the update - take it, this is the build the pause was for. Your key carries over: the same one is still in My Apps and you do not need a new one. One thing to be straight about - the thirty days run from the day you first claimed the key, not from this build, so if you have been testing since August you have less than thirty left. New here? Thirty days from the moment you download. Both builds changed shape: Windows is a zip the Hub unpacks itself, so nothing goes into Program Files, and the Mac build is a proper .pkg installer now rather than a zip. There are two Mac builds now. Apple silicon needs macOS 11 or newer; the Intel one goes back to 10.13 High Sierra, which covers most Intel Macs from around 2009 on. The Hub knows which machine it is running on and offers the right one by itself - in My Apps the two are labelled, so take the one that matches your Mac.

news.title: HarmonieMD: walk into rehearsal already knowing your part
news.body: A voice note has no isolation. A YouTube link has no parts. A Drive folder has no structure. And nobody is installing a DAW to learn an alto line. HarmonieMD gives every singer their own harmony track to solo, slow to 85% without changing pitch, and loop until the bar lands. For the director it is a real multi-track studio underneath, with non-destructive takes and audio latency that is measured rather than estimated. Songs download once, so rehearsal never depends on the church WiFi. Free for teams up to five. Not ready to download yet; the Hub will say the day it is.

studio_news.subject: What's new at Amanorsac Studio
studio_news.heading: What's new at the studio
studio_news.intro: A short note from the studio. A lot has changed over the last few weeks, so here it all is in one place.

items.title: A new website
items.text: The whole site has a new look, and every app has a proper page now: what it does, what it costs and how to get it.

items.title: Chordlight 88 2.0
items.text: See every chord you play, then record it and make the lesson video in one step. Early-bird price on 2.0: $24, normally $48.

items.title: Stem Sorter, new
items.text: Quickly import session files into your mix template, so the session is laid out before you start mixing.

items.title: Nebula Tide 2.0.2
items.text: MIDI learn is easier, and textures and FX have their own volume. It runs on Windows, Mac and Android.

items.title: The Studio Bundle
items.text: A Fender Studio Pro template built for your church, four of the studio's plug-ins, and a setup session where we put it all on your machine with you. $250.

items.title: Creators wanted
items.text: The store is looking for producers and musicians to sell multitracks, stems, pads and loops for worship teams. Apply, or message the studio on WhatsApp first.

items.title: Paying from Ghana?

announcement.headline: Chordlight 88 now records, and draws the lesson video for you.
announcement.body: Press Rec and the take is saved as MIDI, 24-bit WAV, or a .chordlight file that reopens with the lights and the audio together. Press Video and the app draws its own 1080p clip, with your title, a backdrop and the chord trail, without a screen recorder. Free for everyone who has Chordlight 88; new at $24 while the early bird lasts.
